necessary_context.applies_to: Interpretation of derivative products; does not change the diagnostic norm convention
necessary_context.content: Section 2.1 uses Euclidean vector norm and Frobenius matrix norm. The mixed derivative g_xy is a d by d' matrix, with entry partial^2 g/(partial x_i partial y_j). The local diagnostic separately uses spectral operator norm.
necessary_context.name: Norms and mixed derivative

necessary_context.applies_to: Source context for Proposition 1 and general bilevel ALSET
necessary_context.content: For all z1=(x1,y1), z2=(x2,y2), f, grad f, grad g and Hessian g are respectively ell_f0, ell_f1, ell_g1 and ell_g2 Lipschitz in the displayed norms. For each fixed x, g(x,.) is mu_g-strongly convex, mu_g>0; kappa=ell_g1/mu_g. Stochastic grad f, grad g and Hessian g are unbiased, with variance bounds sigma_f^2, sigma_g1^2, sigma_g2^2 respectively. These assumptions concern the expected functions; they do not explicitly impose the same spectral bounds on every stochastic Hessian.
necessary_context.name: Assumptions 1–3

necessary_context.applies_to: Motivation and dimensions of Eq.(10); not an independently verified Proposition 1 record
necessary_context.content: Proposition 1 states, under Assumptions 1–3, grad F(x)=grad_x f(x,y*(x))-g_xy(x,y*(x))[g_yy(x,y*(x))]^{-1}grad_y f(x,y*(x)); grad F and y* are Lipschitz with constants L_F and L_y. Eq.(7) defines the analogous surrogate at a general y. The supplementary proof and formulas for these constants were not read.
